concerns: The headline gains are established on a small author-constructed benchmark of 50 cases with only 10-15 cases per depth stratum, and the authors explicitly state that larger independent evaluations are needed to establish robustness [E96340e533c113cf7-B0003, E96340e533c113cf7-B0035, E96340e533c113cf7-B0051].

Retained experimental records are incomplete: the number of evaluation runs per configuration and the size of the double-annotated subset were not preserved, and action-decision evaluation plus a premise-gate ablation were omitted because their aggregation could not be reconstructed [E96340e533c113cf7-B0038, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054].

No significance tests were run, so the reported depth-wise differences and public-benchmark comparisons do not establish reliable superiority or even absence of degradation [E96340e533c113cf7-B0046, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054].

Relation typing, counterfactual verification, and alternative-support assessment all use the same LLM, so their errors can be correlated, and the manuscript provides no independent guarantee against correlated errors across proposal, verification, and support assessment [E96340e533c113cf7-B0051, E96340e533c113cf7-B0055].
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the conceptual framework for dependency-aware cascade revision is coherent and interesting, the scientific foundation is weakened by critical reporting gaps admitted by the authors, including incomplete retained experimental records, unpreserved evaluation run counts, and a benchmark size of only 50 cases [E96340e533c113cf7-B0038, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054]. Given these uncertainties and the small sample scale, uncertain is the scientifically prudent judgment.

must stay consistent with a world that keeps
changing. When an upstream fact changes,

and actions derived from it remain accepted,
even though they have lost their support. We
therefore formulate dependency-aware state re-
vision, which asks not only what changed but
also which dependent states should no longer
be trusted. To address it, StateGraph maintains
an evolving state dependency graph whose
edges are recovered from interaction histories.

each candidate edge is tested by asking whether
the dependent state would survive the loss of its
premise, which separates support dependence

Public Memory Benchmarks
This supplementary evaluation checks whether
adding dependency revision coincides with lower
performance on standard long-term memory tasks.
Using State Answer Accuracy, StateGraph scores
52.0% on STALE versus CUPMem's 51.7%, and
53.9% on LongMemEval (Wu et al., 2025) versus
Mem0's 51.3%. On MemoryAgentBench it scores
36.6%, below A-MEM's 43.1% and above CUP-
Mem's 28.1%. Its point estimates are comparable
to or higher than those of the evaluated baselines
on five of the six benchmarks. We did not run
significance tests, so these results do not establish
the absence of degradation. Appendix A, Table 7,
reports all six benchmarks.

blocking_reasons: The headline gains are established on a small author-constructed benchmark of 50 cases with only 10-15 cases per depth stratum, and the authors explicitly state that larger independent evaluations are needed to establish robustness [E96340e533c113cf7-B0003, E96340e533c113cf7-B0035, E96340e533c113cf7-B0051].

Retained experimental records are incomplete: the number of evaluation runs per configuration and the size of the double-annotated subset were not preserved, and action-decision evaluation plus a premise-gate ablation were omitted because their aggregation could not be reconstructed [E96340e533c113cf7-B0038, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054].

No significance tests were run, so the reported depth-wise differences and public-benchmark comparisons do not establish reliable superiority or even absence of degradation [E96340e533c113cf7-B0046, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054].

Relation typing, counterfactual verification, and alternative-support assessment all use the same LLM, so their errors can be correlated, and the manuscript provides no independent guarantee against correlated errors across proposal, verification, and support assessment [E96340e533c113cf7-B0051, E96340e533c113cf7-B0055].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: StateChangeBench outcomes are scored against human gold annotations, and supplementary results are reported on six public long-term memory benchmarks [E96340e533c113cf7-B0036, E96340e533c113cf7-B0046, E96340e533c113cf7-B0079].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are measured by Impact-F1, over-/under-invalidation, and CVR against human-annotated gold labels on StateChangeBench, plus State Answer Accuracy on public benchmarks [E96340e533c113cf7-B0036, E96340e533c113cf7-B0043, E96340e533c113cf7-B0046, E96340e533c113cf7-B0084].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system's dependency graph is shaped by DeepSeek-v4-Flash through candidate discovery, relation typing, counterfactual verification, and alternative-support assessment, with no reported training or tuning loop [E96340e533c113cf7-B0026, E96340e533c113cf7-B0038, E96340e533c113cf7-B0055].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported margins on StateChangeBench (e.g., 26.0 point margin over CUPMem at depth 3+) align with the stated numbers, but generalizability is limited by the tiny 50-case dataset, single-LLM pipeline dependencies, and lack of statistical significance testing [E96340e533c113cf7-B0003, E96340e533c113cf7-B0044, E96340e533c113cf7-B0046, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054]. Broader public benchmark evaluation shows only modest, mixed results across standard memory tasks [E96340e533c113cf7-B0046].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation relies heavily on StateChangeBench, a small author-constructed benchmark of 50 cases with only 10 to 15 cases per depth stratum [E96340e533c113cf7-B0010, E96340e533c113cf7-B0035]. The authors acknowledge that retained experimental records are incomplete, failing to preserve the number of pooled evaluation runs or the sample size of the double-annotated agreement subset, and omitting action-decision results due to lost records [E96340e533c113cf7-B0038, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes on StateChangeBench are evaluated against human gold-standard status annotations, and supplementary tests are conducted across six public benchmarks including LongMemEval and STALE [E96340e533c113cf7-B0036, E96340e533c113cf7-B0046, E96340e533c113cf7-B0079].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Impact-F1 and over-/under-invalidation measured against human-annotated gold target sets and dependency closures on StateChangeBench, as well as external accuracy on standard long-term memory benchmarks [E96340e533c113cf7-B0036, E96340e533c113cf7-B0043, E96340e533c113cf7-B0046, E96340e533c113cf7-B0084].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Heuristic and prompt-driven in-context prompting utilizing DeepSeek-v4-Flash for candidate discovery, relation typing, and counterfactual verification [E96340e533c113cf7-B0026, E96340e533c113cf7-B0038, E96340e533c113cf7-B0092].

primary.limitations: The manuscript transparently admits severe record-keeping limitations, including unrecorded evaluation run counts, unknown annotation sample sizes, omitted action-decision evaluations, and potential correlated errors from using the same LLM for candidate proposal and verification [E96340e533c113cf7-B0051, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054, E96340e533c113cf7-B0055].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is explicitly articulated, detailing bounded candidate discovery, counterfactual dependency verification into strict/weak/none categories, and conservative cascade revision tracking alternative support [E96340e533c113cf7-B0009, E96340e533c113cf7-B0026, E96340e533c113cf7-B0030]. Prompt structures, schemas, and algorithmic routines are thoroughly documented [E96340e533c113cf7-B0030, E96340e533c113cf7-B0088].
primary.quality_rationale: While the conceptual framework for dependency-aware cascade revision is coherent and interesting, the scientific foundation is weakened by critical reporting gaps admitted by the authors, including incomplete retained experimental records, unpreserved evaluation run counts, and a benchmark size of only 50 cases [E96340e533c113cf7-B0038, E96340e533c113cf7-B0054]. Given these uncertainties and the small sample scale, uncertain is the scientifically prudent judgment.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces dependency-aware state revision for long-term agent memory, implemented via StateGraph which recovers and counterfactually verifies latent dependencies to propagate state invalidations, and introduces StateChangeBench, a 50-case controlled cascade benchmark [E96340e533c113cf7-B0002, E96340e533c113cf7-B0009, E96340e533c113cf7-B0010].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Held-out benchmark results include objective token F1 and retrieval completeness metrics alongside task-specific ground-truth accuracy and separate judge scores, and the reported gains are directionally consistent across these measures.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are reported on held-out benchmarks (MemSyco-Bench, MemTrapBench, LoCoMo, LoCoMo-Refined) using task accuracy, token F1, sycophancy rate, retrieval completeness, and separate LLM-judge scores.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The reasoning-state policy is trained with GRPO using reward gains computed by a task-specific evaluator over a frozen Qwen3-8B personal agent on synthetic training instances derived from FEVER, SciFact, and PersonaMem.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical gains in memory retrieval completeness and task-appropriate reasoning align well with the presented quantitative results, error analyses, and ablation experiments.
primary.evaluation_assessment: EvoMemState is thoroughly evaluated against 9 competitive baselines across four distinct benchmarks (MemSyco-Bench, MemTrapBench, LoCoMo, and LoCoMo-Refined) under two backbones (Qwen3-8B and GPT-4o-mini). Metrics span accuracy, token-level F1, sycophancy rate, complete retrieval rate, and Acc@complete, backed by extensive ablations and cross-system transfer analyses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations on held-out benchmarks include objective token F1, task-specific ground-truth accuracy, and retrieval completeness metrics alongside separate judge models across distinct benchmark datasets.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out evaluation benchmarks (MemSyco-Bench, MemTrapBench, LoCoMo, LoCoMo-Refined) measuring token F1, task accuracy, safety scores, and separate external LLM judges.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: GRPO training of the reasoning state policy using relative reward gains over a frozen personal agent evaluated on answer score on synthetic/QA training instances derived from FEVER, SciFact, and PersonaMem.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations, specifically noting the focus on text-based dialogues and the need to expand the ontology and memory mechanisms to multimodal user artifacts (documents, images).
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is explicitly formulated, describing the incremental construction of an ontology graph (CREATE, MERGE, SPLIT, SUPERSEDES, CONFLICTS_WITH) alongside training a separate policy model (Qwen3-4B-Instruct) using GRPO with task-specific reward relative to a frozen agent baseline.
primary.quality_rationale: The study addresses a clear problem in agent memory architectures with an elegant formulation separating persistent facts, relational states, and policy-driven reasoning states. The experimental evaluation is rigorous, multi-faceted, and well-controlled with multiple established benchmarks and extensive baseline comparisons.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces EvoMemState, a long-term memory framework for LLM personal agents that augments persistent facts with relational states (capturing updates and conflicts via an ontology) and a reasoning state policy trained via reinforcement learning (GRPO) to direct memory applicability and priority at inference time.

harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools,
or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and
redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can
be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup. In
ROBOARCHITECT, a coding model observes a robot's rollouts, diagnoses failures,
and iteratively revises the harness around the frozen policy. The harness evolves on

Scaling cap of iterations.As shown in Figs. 10 to 12, harness performance on the training
episodes improves consistently across iterations. However, this work uses a fixed maximum of 5
optimization iterations (§4.1). More iterations may yield further gains, but the point at which returns
saturate remains to be explored. Nevertheless, even with a moderate budget of only 5 iterations (§B),
ROBOARCHITECTachieves substantial gains that transfer to held-out settings.
More complex manipulation.A natural next step is extending ROBOARCHITECTto tasks with
richer contact dynamics, such as dexterous in-hand manipulation or tool use, where the space of
failure modes is larger than in pick-and-place. The range of control routines and memory structures
that automated evolution can discover in these settings is an interesting open question.
Sim-to-real transfer.All evaluations run in simulation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final reported outcomes are evaluated on held-out splits not accessed during harness optimization, and are additionally compared against benchmark-finetuned policy baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective task success rate and progress scores measured in standard simulator environments on strictly held-out unseen scenes, unseen tasks, or standard benchmark episodes.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Simulated task completion success/progress on designated training-split rollout episodes, used by the coding model to diagnose failures and accept candidate harness revisions.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical gains strongly align with claims: iterative harness optimization improves unseen scene success from 9.7% to 43.3% and unseen task success from 12.7% to 40.2%, often outperforming full finetuning in out-of-domain scenarios.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is extensive across five benchmarks (LIBERO-Pro-10, RoboCerebra, VLABench, SimplerEnv WidowX/Google, and RoboCasa-365) and seven base policies, rigorously testing held-out generalization on unseen scenes and unseen tasks. The reporting includes comparisons against bare policies, one-shot harness generation, finetuned policy checkpoints, and cross-embodiment unified harnesses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final reported outcomes are evaluated on strictly held-out splits (unseen scenes and unseen tasks) not accessed during harness optimization, as well as against benchmark-finetuned policy baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective task success rate and progress scores measured in standard simulator environments on strictly held-out unseen scenes, unseen tasks, or standard benchmark episodes.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Simulated task completion success/progress on designated training-split rollout episodes, used by Claude Opus 5 to diagnose failures and accept candidate harness revisions.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently document limitations, including an exploration cap of five iterations, evaluation confined to simulated manipulation environments without physical hardware testing, and focus on pick-and-place/basic manipulation tasks rather than complex in-hand dexterity.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the pass-through base harness, tool integrations, empirical acceptance criterion on training rollouts, and the persistent memory mechanism. The multi-iteration revision process enables the coding agent to refine perception routines, coordinate motion recovery, and adapt to specific robotic embodiments.
primary.quality_rationale: RoboArchitect provides a well-substantiated contribution to embodied agent design. The experimental validation strictly separates training episodes used for code evolution from held-out evaluation splits (unseen scenes and unseen tasks) scored using objective benchmark task success metrics.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RoboArchitect, an automated framework that uses a frontier coding model to iteratively diagnose execution traces and rewrite Python agent harnesses—incorporating auxiliary vision/language tools and emergent persistent memory—around frozen VLA robot policies without weight updates.
